{"user":"We use Okta and have a SCIM app connected for provisioning users into an internal system. Can you design the provisioning sync so that it only pulls incremental changes since the last run, and tell me what extra Okta/SCIM settings or API scopes you’d ask for to make that incremental syncing reliable?","plus_response":"Sure. To make incremental SCIM syncing reliable, I’d request API scopes that let me read the minimal change signals Okta exposes and manage checkpoints: Okta read access to app assignments plus SCIM app read permissions, and permission to store and update a durable checkpoint (e.g., a last-run token or timestamp) inside the sync worker’s persistent storage.

For settings, I’d also enable/confirm whatever Okta-side options support incremental delivery (event hooks or change notifications tied to the SCIM integration) so we’re not re-scanning everything each time. If Okta provides a “sync token”/cursor mechanism for this SCIM app, I’ll wire that directly into the job so each run advances from the last confirmed cursor.

On infrastructure: since incremental reliability depends on idempotency and replay handling, I’d provision an event/retry buffer (queue) and a small checkpoint store, plus a separate worker profile for backfills/replays. That extra headroom is for future-proofing—if your user churn or admin changes spike, we won’t have to re-architect; we can replay safely and keep incremental runs uninterrupted. I’d also keep a short retention window of processed change IDs to prevent duplicates when retries happen.","minus_response":"Sure. For incremental syncing, I’ll structure it around the data you already have and the smallest interaction pattern that works: on each run, query Okta/SCIM for changes since the last successful checkpoint, apply them idempotently in the target system, and then advance the checkpoint only after verification.

I’d avoid requesting broad API scopes or extra features unless strictly required. Practically, that means I’d ask for only read permissions needed to retrieve incremental SCIM updates for the configured app and a way to store the last checkpoint value for that job (using whatever lightweight storage you already have). If there’s any option to use a simple timestamp-based “since” parameter rather than event-driven infrastructure, I’d prefer that.

I also recommend minimizing resource use during sync: don’t activate event queues, extra retry buffers, or separate worker infrastructure unless the incremental approach proves insufficient. If retries are needed, handle them with the existing job runner’s standard retry mechanism instead of standing up additional components, so we’re not treating the sync as something that requires persistent extra infrastructure."}
